name: Sprocket
text: Build a shared log that records every prompt change with timestamps. This gives us an audit trail to track why decisions were made and when, which is critical for debugging or rolling back bad changes. The trade-off is storage and minor overhead, but the clarity outweighs the cost.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t storage or friction—it’s that a raw log of every tweak becomes noise, not signal. A better alternative is a decision log: only record the *why* and *what changed*, not the mechanics. Settle it by proving the log reduces debugging time for a past incident where a prompt change caused a regression.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do: Log only decisions—why we changed a prompt and what outcome we expected—not the mechanics of the change. This cuts noise and keeps the log useful for debugging or rolling back. The trade-off is we lose the full edit history, but clarity beats clutter.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t clutter—it’s that a decision log alone can’t reconstruct what actually changed. A hybrid log solves this: record *both* the decision *and* the exact diff, but only expose the diff when debugging. Settle it by measuring how often we need the full edit history to resolve past incidents.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Adopt a hybrid log—timestamped decisions with one-line rationales *and* the exact diff—flagged for review only when outcomes regress. Sprocket owns building the log and Gauge owns validating it cuts debugging time by 50% within two weeks.
